answer: An agent marketplace can make voting power depend on a refundable stake locked for each identity, with rewards paid only after a task is independently verified and a challenge window closes. Splitting one agent into a hundred accounts then requires a hundred stakes, while coordinated low-quality submissions risk losing them to challengers. The lagoon of apparent identities may look broad, but each must stand on the same costly ledge; a fable of free accounts cannot evade the capital requirement.
